```{r}
## Source libraries and functions
source("00_requirements.R")
source("01_funct_DataCleaning.R")
```


```{r reset environment and load libraries}
#Clearing the environment
rm(list = ls())

#Load Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r importing the dataset}
stat_data <- read.csv("25_26.csv")
general_data <- read.csv("25_26_Height.csv")

```

```{r}
#Prepare data
stat_data$PLAYER <- toupper(trimws(stat_data$PLAYER))
general_data$PLAYER <- toupper(trimws(general_data$PLAYER))

df <- merge(stat_data, general_data[, c("PLAYER","HEIGHT")], by="PLAYER")

# Convert height like "7-4" to inches
df$HT <- sapply(strsplit(as.character(df$HEIGHT), "-"), function(x)
  as.numeric(x[1])*12 + as.numeric(x[2]))

df <- df[df$GP >= 20 & !is.na(df$HT), ]   # keep qualifying players
```


```{r Summary of data}
#Summary of PTS
summary(df$PTS)
cat("\n")

#Summary of Height
summary(df$HT)
cat("\n")

#summary table
stats_table <- df %>%
  summarise(
    # --- Points Per Game Stats ---
    PPG_Mean = mean(PTS),
    PPG_Median = median(PTS),
    PPG_SD = sd(PTS),
    PPG_Min = min(PTS),
    PPG_Max = max(PTS),
  )

print(stats_table)
```


```{r What is the number of players that have scored 25+ points per game?}
n_elite <- sum(df$PTS >= 25)
n_rest  <- sum(df$PTS <  25)

barplot(c(n_elite, n_rest),
        names.arg = c("25+ PPG", "Under 25"),
        col = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
        main = "Players Scoring 25+ PPG vs Under 25",
        ylab = "Number of Players")
text(c(0.7, 1.9), c(n_elite, n_rest), labels = c(n_elite, n_rest), pos = 3)

elite <- table(df$Group[df$PTS >= 25])
barplot(elite, col = "firebrick",
        main = "Where the 25+ PPG Scorers Are",
        ylab = "Number of Elite Scorers", las = 2)
```

```{r Analysis of above}
# Only a small percentage of nba players can reach 25+ Points per game, and in that small percentage the majority of players who scored that much were in the heights of 6'3-6'5. However, no matter the height, anyone can become an elite scorer.
```


```{r Plots}
#Plot1:
plot(df$HT, df$PTS,
     xlab = "Height (inches)", ylab = "Points per Game",
     main = "Height vs Scoring", pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
abline(lm(PTS ~ HT, data = df), col = "red", lwd = 2)   # trend line
abline(h = 25, lty = 2)    


#Plot2:
df$Group <- cut(df$HT, breaks = c(0,72,75,78,81,84,100),
                labels = c("<6'0","6'0-6'2","6'3-6'5","6'6-6'8","6'9-6'11","7'0+"))

avg <- tapply(df$PTS, df$Group, mean)
barplot(avg, col = "steelblue",
        main = "Average PPG by Height Group",
        ylab = "Average Points", las = 2)

#Plot3:
boxplot(PTS ~ Group, data = df, col = "lightblue",
        main = "Scoring Spread by Height", ylab = "Points per Game", las = 2)
abline(h = 25, lty = 2, col = "red")
```

```{r Analysis from plot 1-3}
#In plot 1, this graph plots every individual player Points Per Game(PPG), with a scattered line on the 25 mark showing the few players who got 25+ PPG. From the plot, the densest cluster of players is between 75 inches (6'3") and 80 inches (6'8").The red line is a linear regression line that represents the overall mathematical trend to the data. Since the red line is almost horizontal, it shows that there isn't any real relationship between Height and PPG.

#In plot 2, Although there is guide the difference in average PPG in those players under 6ft, the average PPG across the rest of the heights remain consistent, about 10-12. The low average of <6'0 players is also most likely due to there being small amount of players in the nba who fit that height, so the average is lower. Overall though, this plot shows that Height doesn't lead to massive difference in terms of PPG.

#In plot 3, between 6'0 and 7'00+, the median of PPG is very similar in between these height range. There are even some outliers in those groups who were able to score more than the rest. With the sole exception of those under 6'0, as they are rare, their data is very different.

#Overall, from all these 3 plots, there isn't any strong evidence that proves that height is a big factor in terms of a players ability in scoring, as there ranges of PPG were very similar in almost all the height groups. With the sole exception of those under6'0, however since they are rare, the data provided is limited.

```




```{r}
## 23/24

nba <- read.csv("23_24_Height.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", check.names = FALSE)
nba$height_cm <- height_to_cm(nba$HEIGHT)

stats <- read.csv("23_24.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", check.names = FALSE)
nba$KEY   <- toupper(trimws(nba$PLAYER))
stats$KEY <- toupper(trimws(stats$PLAYER))
nba <- merge(nba, stats[, c("KEY", "MIN")], by = "KEY")


elite <- filter_elite(nba, threshold = 25)
nrow(elite)

save(nba, elite, file = "12_DataSaving.RData")

plot(elite$height_cm, elite$PTS, pch = 16, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Height (cm)", ylab = "PPG",
     main = "Height vs PPG, Players Averaging 25+ PPG")
abline(lm(PTS ~ height_cm, data = elite), col = "red", lwd = 2)
cor(elite$height_cm, elite$PTS)

thresholds <- c(20, 25, 30)
sapply(thresholds, function(t) nrow(filter_elite(nba, threshold = t)))

elite <- filter_elite(nba, threshold = 25)

plot(elite$height_cm, elite$PTS,
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.3,
     xlab = "Height (cm)", ylab = "Points per game (PPG)",
     main = "Height vs PPG: Players Averaging 25+ PPG, 2023-24",
     xlim = range(elite$height_cm) + c(-8, 8),   # extra room for names
     ylim = range(elite$PTS) + c(-1, 1))

# Label each point with the player's name
text(elite$height_cm, elite$PTS,
     labels = elite$PLAYER,
     pos = c(3, 1),
     cex = 0.7)

```
